overview: Both conserve momentum, but only elastic collisions also conserve total kinetic energy.
genZNote: Momentum's always invited to the conservation party — kinetic energy only shows up if the collision's elastic.

aspects.label: Kinetic Energy Conserved?
aspects.valueA: Yes — total KE before equals total KE after.
aspects.valueB: No — some KE converts to heat, sound, or deformation.

aspects.label: Real-World Closeness
aspects.valueA: Collisions between hard billiard balls or gas molecules approximate this closely.
aspects.valueB: A perfectly inelastic case is two objects sticking together after collision (maximum KE loss).
